Article Title: Oil remains above $100 per barrel as traders await potential US-Iran talks
Article Text:
Oil prices remain above $100 per barrel

Oil prices climbed back above the $100-a-barrel mark as tensions in the Middle East continued to intensify, keeping markets on edge. Brent crude rose 0.51% to $100.80 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) gained 0.43% to $92.77, on Tuesday.The rise, however, was limited as traders weighed signs of possible US-Iran talks against the continuing tensions in the Gulf. Oil prices had fallen recently, so traders who were hoping for a further drop were now cutting those bets as they waited for clearer signs from the diplomatic efforts.The US and Iran traded threats on Sunday, even as US President Donald Trump said that he was open to meeting Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, who is expected to travel to New York this week for the UN General Assembly.Meanwhile, Iran has also signalled that it could return to negotiations, with the country conveying conditions to mediators over the weekend for re-engaging in talks, Al Jazeera reported, citing Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei. At the same time, developments elsewhere in the region continued to keep pressure on the oil market.Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis said they had carried out attacks on Riyadh and a Saudi Aramco facility in Yanbu.The group has also intensified efforts to cut off Saudi-backed forces from the Red Sea coast.The disruption has also affected the movement of oil through the region. Saudi Aramco has increased exports through the Strait of Hormuz after attacks on its East-West Pipeline forced it to stop some shipments through Yanbu.Tanker tracking data showed that Aramco loaded around 14 million barrels of crude on seven supertankers inside the Gulf on Sunday.As the conflict continues, traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has dropped sharply. Only 12 commodity vessels passed through the waterway over the weekend, compared with 35 during the previous weekend, according to shipping data cited by Reuters.The decline came as tensions between the US and Iran continued for over 6 months now, with the two sides remaining in a stalemate.
Article Summary: Brent crude rose 0.51% to $100.80 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) gained 0.43%. The rise was limited as traders weighed signs of possible US-Iran talks against the continuing tensions in the Gulf.

Article Title: Red Sea hit, Hormuz choked: How Saudi Arabia has kept its oil exports moving
Article Text:
Saudi Arabia ramps up Gulf oil exports after pipeline attack

Saudi shipments show signs of recovery

Hormuz traffic remains below normal

Saudi Arabia has ramped up crude exports through the Strait of Hormuz after attacks on its East-West oil pipeline disrupted a key alternative route for the Kingdom’s exports.Saudi Aramco loaded about 14 million barrels of crude on seven very large crude carriers (VLCCs) inside the Mideast Gulf on Sunday, according to TankerTrackers.com data. Satellite images seen by Reuters also appeared to show seven tankers near Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura port on the same day.The pipeline attacks forced Saudi Arabia to shut its East-West oil pipeline on September 13, halting crude loadings at the kingdom's Yanbu oil port on the Red Sea. Since September 16, there have been no visible oil loadings from Yanbu.Following the disruption, Aramco cancelled some crude cargo sales to European clients while increasing sales to Asia of crude loaded at its eastern ports inside the Strait of Hormuz.The rise in Gulf loadings adds to signs of a partial recovery in Saudi crude shipments. In a note cited by Reuters, JP Morgan analysts said Saudi oil was moving through the Strait of Hormuz averaged 2.9 million barrels per day over the previous six days, up from just 700,000 bpd in August.Kpler data showed that 22 tankers, mostly VLCCs, carrying 42 million barrels of crude exited the Strait of Hormuz in the week of September 13.Saudi Arabia and Iraq each accounted for 43% of the volume.Saudi Arabia has also sold about 60 million barrels of crude from its Ras Tanura port inside the Strait of Hormuz for loading through ship-to-ship transfers at Oman's Sohar port this month and next, trade sources told Reuters last week.The increase in shipments came as expectations of higher Saudi supplies weighed on oil prices on Monday, pushing the Brent benchmark below $100 a barrel for the first time since September 9.While Saudi crude shipments have increased, overall traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains sharply lower as tensions in the Gulf continue, with the US and Iran in stalemate.Shipping data showed that 17 commodity vessels transited the strait over the weekend, down from 37 a week earlier.Visible traffic through the strait, which handled a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas before the war, has fallen to a trickle. Middle Eastern producers, however, continue to export oil on tankers travelling with their transponders switched off.Among trackable ships, five vessels exited the strait on Sunday, while two smaller oil tankers entered the Gulf, according to provisional data from analytics firm Kpler.The vessels that exited included the very large crude carrier Pinios, two tankers carrying refined oil products and two empty carriers for bulk goods and gas.At the Bab el-Mandeb Strait at the southern end of the Red Sea, 51 vessels made the crossing, with 33 exiting over the weekend. These included an Aframax-sized tanker carrying about 700,000 barrels of Saudi crude, according to Kpler data.That was down from 57 vessels during the previous weekend.Meanwhile, chaos in the Middle East has continued to disrupt global oil supplies for over six months now, with no peaceful resolution in sight.
Article Summary: Saudi Arabia has ramped up crude exports through the Strait of Hormuz after attacks on its East-West oil pipeline disrupted a key alternative route for the Kingdom’s exports. Saudi Aramco loaded about 14 million barrels of crude on seven very large crude carriers (VLCCs) inside the Mideast Gulf on Sunday.

Article Title: ‘Resolve issues through dialogue’: Government urges bank employees to call off September 28-30 strike
Article Text:
File photo: Members of United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) hold placards during the nationwide strike for various demands (ANI Photo)

Five-day banking demand remains

Government lists measures for bank staff

Banks prepare for possible disruption

The finance ministry on Monday urged bank employees to refrain from resorting to strikes and resolve their remaining demands through dialogue, saying most concerns raised by unions had been substantially addressed.The appeal comes ahead of a three-day nationwide strike called by the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) from September 28 to 30. The unions are primarily seeking implementation of a five-day banking week and withdrawal of the Performance Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme.The government said the PLI scheme had already been kept in abeyance earlier this month following discussions with unions, while the remaining demand for a five-day workweek continues to be examined."Given that most concerns of the unions have been substantially addressed, that the remaining demand continues to be examined, and that the Government continues to proactively introduce welfare measures for the banking workforce, bank employees are urged to refrain from resorting to strikes, work towards resolving issues through dialogue, and ensure that banking services remain uninterrupted," the finance ministry said in a statement.The proposed strike follows a one-day nationwide strike held on September 11 over the unions' demands, despite what the government described as sustained conciliatory engagement.The government said the September 28-30 strike would coincide with the half-yearly closing of banks on September 30, a period significant for reconciliation, provisioning, treasury and market operations.The strike would also follow the weekend, potentially resulting in an effective five-day closure of branch-based banking services. The government said this could affect customers, businesses, government transactions and international banking operations.An indefinite strike has also been proposed from October 26 over the remaining demand for a five-day workweek.The finance ministry said banking services were relied upon by citizens and that the remaining Saturdays, other than the second and fourth Saturdays, continued to provide an opportunity for customers to access banking services.The government said it had introduced several measures aimed at improving the working environment, transparency and welfare of bank employees.These include increases in salary and allowances, fixation of new pay scales for all cadres, a higher Staff Welfare Fund and an increase in executive posts at the levels of assistant general manager, deputy general manager, general manager and chief general manager.Public sector banks recruited around 4.82 lakh employees between FY2014-15 and FY2025-26, with recruitment doubling over the last three years, according to the government.As of July 1, 95.84% of officer positions and 92% of subordinate and award staff positions were filled.Other measures listed by the government include improved transfer and promotion processes, special leave provisions for women employees, revised family pensions, enhanced medical insurance for retirees and a higher conveyance allowance for employees with disabilities.The government has also begun negotiations for the upcoming Bipartite Settlement ahead of the November 2027 deadline, with the stated aim of ensuring timely revision of bankers' salaries and allowances.The proposed strike has prompted banks to advise customers to complete important branch-related transactions before the strike period.State Bank of India said it was taking steps to continue providing essential banking services during the proposed strike and asked customers to use alternative channels, including ATMs, customer service centres, internet banking, mobile banking, UPI and other digital services.Union Bank of India similarly said it was working to maintain essential banking services, while cautioning that branch operations could be affected during the three-day strike.The government said public sector banks play a key role in financial inclusion, digital banking, financial literacy and rural outreach, and stressed the importance of maintaining uninterrupted banking services while the outstanding demand is addressed through dialogue.
Article Summary: Finance ministry urges bank employees to refrain from resorting to strikes. Appeal comes ahead of a three-day nationwide strike called by the United Forum of Bank Unions. Unions are seeking implementation of a five-day banking week and withdrawal of the Performance Linked Incentive scheme.

Article Title: India-New Zealand FTA kicks in from October 20 with duty-free access for all Indian exports
Article Text:
India-New Zealand trade deal to come into force on Dussehra (representative image)

India gets duty-free access for all exports

Bilateral trade rises 49%

Ministers hail agreement amid global trade uncertainty

The India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA) will come into force on October 20, coinciding with Dussehra, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said on Monday, with India securing duty-free access for 100 per cent of its exports to New Zealand.Goyal made the announcement during a virtual interaction with New Zealand trade and investment minister Todd McClay in New Delhi.The agreement was signed in the capital on April 27 after negotiations between the two countries concluded in nine months.“I’m delighted that we are taking forward the next important milestone in our bilateral economic partnership: the entry into force of the India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement, which will come into force on the auspicious occasion of Dussehra on 20th October 2026,” Goyal said.Under the agreement, 100 per cent of Indian exports to New Zealand will receive duty-free access from the day the FTA comes into force.New Zealand, meanwhile, will eliminate or significantly reduce tariffs on about 95 per cent of its exports to India, including wine, kiwi fruit and apples, according to Reuters.The agreement also includes provisions to ease mobility rules for students and workers. Wellington has committed to investing $20 billion in India over the next 15 years.New Zealand high commissioner to India Patrick John Rata described the pact as a “huge” development for both countries.“It is huge for both countries. I think an FTA works well because the two countries have decided to trust each other, and that is what has happened with New Zealand and India. We put trust in the vision of our two countries coming closer together over the next period,” Rata told news agency ANI.Government data showed that India-New Zealand merchandise trade increased from $873 million in 2023-24 to $1.3 billion in 2024-25, registering 49 per cent growth.India's merchandise exports to New Zealand rose 32 per cent to $711 million in 2024-25. India's services exports to New Zealand also increased 13 per cent in 2024 to $634 million, with travel, IT and business services among the major sectors.India recorded higher exports than imports from New Zealand in 2024-25, maintaining a positive trade balance.Prime Minister Narendra Modi and New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon have set an aspirational goal of doubling bilateral trade in goods and services to almost Rs 35,000 crore over the next four or five years, Goyal said.The two leaders have committed to doubling bilateral trade by 2030.Goyal said political momentum for the economic relationship had also strengthened following visits by Luxon to India and PM Modi to New Zealand in July 2026.PM Modi's visit was the first by an Indian prime minister to New Zealand in four decades.McClay welcomed the agreement coming into force and said both countries could be proud of the deal.“I thank you for your significant commitment, contribution and hard work over the last 2 years. I think both New Zealand and India can be proud of the very high quality agreement that will deliver significant benefits for the citizens of our two countries,” McClay said.He said the ratification of the FTA represented a strengthening of the relationship between the two countries.“At a time when there is uncertainty around the world in trade, we see tariff rates escalating, we see barriers being put up, India and New Zealand show that we can agree to terms that are beneficial for trade and businesses,” McClay said, according to Reuters.McClay said the agreement marked the beginning of a new phase in bilateral relations, covering people-to-people ties, culture, sport, business and investment.The FTA comes into force as India faces changes in global trade, including new US measures targeting countries that purchase Russian oil.India has accelerated efforts to diversify export markets through trade agreements with major economies, including Britain and the European Union.“The entry into force of the India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement will translate this code into concrete economic outcomes,” Goyal said.
Article Summary: India-New Zealand trade deal to come into force on Dussehra. India gets duty- free access for all exports to New Zealand. New Zealand will eliminate or significantly reduce tariffs on about 95 per cent of its exports to India. Wellington has committed to investing $20 billion in India over the next 15 years.

Article Title: Gold prices surge 60% from Rs 98,000 to Rs 1.57 lakh per 10 grams in a year; Ganesh Chaturthi sales fall 15% as buyers switch to lighter jewellery, also buy coins
Article Text:
Jewellers remain hopeful that the moderation in demand will prove temporary as the festive calendar progresses.

Gold prices high

Growing interest in coins

Gold hallmarking charges rise

A huge rise in gold prices from the same time last year has led to a drop in gold sales this Ganesh Chaturthi . Gold sales have declined by around 15% year-on-year in volume terms, with consumers either reducing the quantity they bought or opting for lighter jewellery as a sharp increase in gold prices made purchases more expensive, industry executives said.In Mumbai's spot market on Monday, gold was trading at Rs 1.57 lakh per 10 grams, including 3% goods and services tax. This was around 60% higher than the Rs 98,000 per 10 grams recorded on Ganesh Chaturthi last year, which fell on August 28.“Domestic gold prices have remained at a historic high, which has impacted volume sales. But overall the mood is optimistic, with many people resorting to old gold jewellery exchanges to buy new jewellery, which is mostly lightweight,” said Surendra Mehta, national secretary, India Bullion & Jewellers Association, according to an ET report.Jewellers remain hopeful that the moderation in demand will prove temporary as the festive calendar progresses towards the peak wedding season. Since weddings are also taking place during the festive period, retailers expect buyers to increasingly seek jewellery that can serve multiple purposes, from celebrations and gifting to regular wear.“We are seeing greater interest in diamonds as buyers seek jewellery that is versatile enough for celebrations, gifting and everyday wear,” said Rohan Hemdev, director, Ananya Jewels.Kumar Jain, owner of Umedmal Tilokchand Zaveri, a 100-year-old outlet in Mumbai's Zaveri Bazaar, said demand for bullion in the form of coins and bars had picked up during this year's Ganesh Chaturthi, although volumes remained below last year's level.“Bullion sales in the form of coins and bars have shown traction this Ganesh Chaturthi, even though the volume is lesser than last year.”The increased preference for coins and bars suggests that consumers are still setting aside money for gold during auspicious occasions, but the elevated price of jewellery is making them more cautious about their purchases.The trend also reflects the broader conditions in India's gold market. According to the World Gold Council, the festive season began on a cautious note as the sharp rise in gold prices prompted consumers to adopt a wait-and-watch approach and defer discretionary purchases.Wedding-related demand, however, has remained comparatively resilient, while physical investment demand has stayed steady.There is also growing interest among younger consumers in purchasing jewellery for themselves. Women, in particular, are increasingly buying jewellery to celebrate festivals as well as personal milestones.Hemdev expects festive-season sales to register double-digit growth, helped by wedding demand, rising disposable incomes and evolving consumption habits. He also pointed to the growing role of digital platforms, social media, influencers and celebrity collaborations in making jewellery more aspirational and appealing to younger consumers.“With the ongoing festive season, we expect buying interest to gradually pick up, especially as consumers and jewellery retailers prepare for the period,” said Darshan Desai, CEO, Aspect Bullion & Refinery.In the meantime, the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) has increased the hallmarking fee for gold articles just before the start of the festive season. The charge, which was earlier Rs 45 per gold article, has now been raised to Rs 75. The fee for silver articles, however, remains unchanged at Rs 35.The change was notified through the BIS (Hallmarking) Amendment Regulations, 2026, dated September 14, 2026.BIS hallmarking is the system used to certify the purity of precious metal articles under the Bureau of Indian Standards framework. A hallmarked article carries three important identifiers: the BIS logo, the karat or millesimal fineness and a six-digit alphanumeric Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID) number.Under the amended Schedule IV, jewellers will now be charged Rs 75 for every gold article sent for hallmarking. A minimum charge of Rs 200 will apply to each consignment.There has been no change in the hallmarking fee for silver. Jewellers will continue to pay Rs 35 per silver article to recognised Assaying and Hallmarking Centres (AHCs), with a minimum consignment charge of Rs 150.
Article Summary: Gold sales have declined by around 15% year-on-year in volume terms. In Mumbai's spot market on Monday, gold was trading at Rs 1.57 lakh per 10 grams. The Bureau of Indian Standards has increased the hallmarking fee for gold articles just before the start of the festive season.

Article Title: In major milestone for India’s offshore energy exploration, ONGC strikes gas in Mahanadi Basin, 43 km off Odisha coast; proximity could enable faster monetisation if commercially viable
Article Text:
The discovery was made on September 18 at the MN-DW18-1-H-D well in the Mahanadi Offshore Basin.

ONGC’s gas discovery

Samudra Manthan

In a big breakthrough, Oil and Natural Gas Corp ( ONGC ) has discovered gas in a deepwater well off India's eastern coast. The find is located close enough to Odisha and may potentially enable quicker development if further appraisal establishes that it is commercially viable, the state-run explorer said on Monday.The discovery also comes at a time when ONGC is increasing its focus on frontier offshore acreage. Deepwater discoveries can require substantial investment in appraisal and infrastructure before they can progress to commercial production.For the Mahanadi Basin discovery, ONGC's next phase of work will involve additional reservoir appraisal, evaluation of recoverable resources and a commercial assessment. A decision on development will be taken only after these steps are completed.The discovery was made on September 18 at the MN-DW18-1-H-D well in the Mahanadi Offshore Basin, around 43 km from Konark, as part of ONGC's Samudra Manthan deepwater exploration campaign, the company said in a statement.This was the first well drilled by ONGC in the Mahanadi Basin under the campaign. The well encountered gas at a depth of 1,441-1,452 metres after drilling reached a target depth of 1,623 metres.According to ONGC, the well has continued to flow gas for the past three days and has shown "encouraging flow and reservoir pressure."The company said the discovery will now undergo further appraisal and commercial evaluation.Reacting to the development, Oil minister Hardeep Singh Puri called it a major milestone for India’s offshore energy exploration.ONGC said the well's relatively close location to the Odisha coastline could help bring the discovery into production sooner if it is ultimately found to be commercially viable. The discovery could also potentially be developed alongside other finds in the region by making use of common facilities.The company said such an approach could be supported by the Petroleum and Natural Gas Rules, 2025, which allow deepwater resources in the area to be brought into production using shared infrastructure.The Mahanadi Basin find comes as ONGC steps up exploration activity across India's deepwater basins. The company is seeking to expand domestic hydrocarbon output as India works to reduce its dependence on imports.The well was spudded on July 25 using the drillship Platinum Explorer.The Samudra Manthan National Offshore Exploration Scheme has been designed to tap India's offshore oil and gas potential through a broad-based exploration programme. The initiative will focus on extensive seismic surveys, deepwater exploration, scientific drilling, common offshore infrastructure and the development of an integrated manufacturing ecosystem.The scheme is planned to run through FY 2030-31 and is expected to add more than 600 Million Metric Tons of Oil Equivalent (MMTOE) to India's reserves.A major component of the programme will be the large-scale collection, processing and interpretation of high-quality seismic data to identify offshore hydrocarbon resources. It will also push for faster exploratory drilling in deepwater and ultra-deepwater areas, along with scientific drilling in frontier basins.The scheme also envisages the creation of common offshore production and evacuation infrastructure, which can support the development of resources discovered in offshore areas. Alongside this, an integrated Oil & Gas Manufacturing and Services Zone is proposed.Digital programme management will form another part of the initiative, along with capacity building, adoption of technology, engagement with stakeholders and international outreach.Overall, the programme is expected to bring more than 600 MMTOE into India's reserves, while substantially widening offshore exploration activity and helping increase domestic oil and gas production.The push comes against the backdrop of India's heavy dependence on imported crude oil. Nearly 90% of the country's crude oil requirements are met through imports. This dependence became particularly evident during the US-Iran conflict, when the closure of the Strait of Hormuz exposed India to the risk of an oil and gas supply shock.India moved quickly to diversify its sources of procurement, but the episode also highlighted the limited availability of domestic supply.It is against this backdrop that the Samudra Manthan scheme assumes greater significance.
Article Summary: The discovery was made on September 18 at the MN-DW18-1-H-D well in the Mahanadi Offshore Basin, around 43 km from Konark. The well encountered gas at a depth of 1,441-1,452 metres. The discovery will now undergo further appraisal and commercial evaluation.

Article Title: Wife sold soft drink for Rs 26 instead of Rs 25, Re 1 overcharge led to husband facing case for 13 years; Bombay HC quashes prosecution because wife was shop owner
Article Text:
The high court described the prosecution as “misconceived and misdirected". (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why did the man win the case?

What about the shop owner?

A man working in his wife’s shop faced a thirteen year criminal case for the sale of a cold drink above the maximum retail price. The Bombay High Court has now brought an end to a criminal case that had continued for 13 years against the man.The court has quashed the prosecution, which arose from an allegation that the man had sold a 600-ml bottle of cold drink for Rs 26 even though its MRP was Rs 25.The allegation concerned an overcharge of Re 1. The man was working at his wife's shop when the incident took place.The case originated from an inspection carried out on March 29, 2013, by the Inspector of Legal Metrology at the man’s flour mill and his wife's shop.During the inspection of the shop, the inspector purchased a 600-ml cold drink bottle carrying an MRP of Rs 25. The man allegedly charged Rs 26 for the bottle and issued a bill showing the same amount.The Legal Metrology Inspector subsequently reported the incident to the Assistant Controller of Legal Metrology in a letter dated July 15, 2013. The letter set out what had allegedly taken place during the inspection of the man’s wife's shop on March 29.On the basis of the inspector's report, the government filed a complaint before the Judicial Magistrate First Class, Lanja.The magistrate then ordered criminal proceedings against the man on July 24, 2013. He was accused of violating Rule 18(2) read with Rule 32(2) of The Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011, in Case No. 121 of 2013.The man challenged the proceedings before the Ratnagiri sessions court through Revision Application No. 25 of 2013. However, the sessions court rejected his challenge on September 18, 2014, leaving the criminal prosecution against him intact, according to an ET report.He subsequently approached the Bombay High Court.The man told the court that the inspector had initially visited his flour mill and allegedly demanded a bribe of Rs 5,000 from him in return for allowing him to continue operating the mill. According to the man, he refused to pay the money.He further alleged that after he declined to pay the bribe, the inspector threatened him and made him sign an authority letter. The man said he did not understand the contents of the document because it was written in English.The dispute remained before the courts for years until the Bombay High Court finally intervened.On June 29, 2026, the court quashed the criminal prosecution against the man, bringing the 13-year-old case arising from the Re 1 cold drink bottle overcharge to an end.Anuj Dave, Practice Head (Ahmedabad & Mumbai), Clavius Legal, told ET that the central reason the man succeeded was that the prosecution had proceeded against the wrong individual.The records relied upon by the prosecution itself showed that the cold drink bottle had been sold by the man’s wife, who owned and operated the shop. The man’s role, according to those records, was limited to preparing the bill on his wife's instructions after the sale had taken place.Dave said the high court drew a distinction between preparing an invoice and actually carrying out a sale. In his view, the provision dealing with overcharging applies to the person who sells the product, rather than someone who merely prepares the bill after the transaction. Since the man was not the person who made the sale, the prosecution against him could not be sustained.The high court described the prosecution as “misconceived and misdirected". It also noted that the date appearing on the bill had been altered, with March changed to June, which further cast doubt on the prosecution's case.Dave says: “This ruling does not mean shops can now charge above MRP that remains an offence. All the court clarified is that the person prosecuted must be the one who actually made the sale. Here the shop was the wife’s and the sale was hers; the husband had only written the bill afterwards. You cannot fasten criminal liability on someone simply because he is related to the seller or happened to hand over an invoice.”The judge said: “In my opinion the overwriting even otherwise makes the entire case doubtful.”The court also examined the contents of the Legal Metrology Inspector's letter dated July 15, 2013. The letter stated that the incident had occurred on March 29, 2013 at the shop belonging to the man’s wife, where she was engaged in selling various items.Importantly, the high court noted that the inspector's own account recorded that the cold drink bottle had been sold by the man’s wife from her shop.The court therefore found that the material on record showed the wife had actually made the sale, while the husband had prepared the bill at her direction.On examining the inspector's letter, the court said it was apparent that the transaction had been carried out by the wife. Despite this, the complaint named only the man. His wife was neither accused of any offence nor were proceedings initiated against her.The high court also considered Rule 18(2) of the Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011. The provision states that a retail dealer or any other person, including a manufacturer, packer, importer or wholesale dealer, cannot sell a packaged commodity at a price higher than its retail sale price.The court noted that Rule 18(2) applies to the retail dealer or other person who actually makes the sale. In the circumstances of this case, the person who made the sale was Narvekar's wife.The high court then considered the definition of “sale” under Section 2(r) of the Legal Metrology Act, 2009.The high court found that the prosecution itself was misconceived because the man was not the shop owner and had not actually made the sale. According to the court, he had only prepared the bill, while the transaction was carried out by his wife, who owned the shop.The court also held that preparing a bill on the instructions of the shop owner could not, by itself, be treated as a "sale" within the meaning of Section 2(r) of the Legal Metrology Act, 2009.The judgment does not automatically result in any action against the man’s wife. Dave said the high court did not determine whether she had herself violated the law. Its finding was limited to the fact that the man had been wrongly prosecuted. The court also noted that his wife had never been made an accused in the case.In principle, the authorities could examine the conduct of the person who actually carried out the sale. However, the transaction in question took place back in 2013.Dave says: "A fresh case now would run straight into limitation. This is a fine-only offence with only a short window to prosecute apart from the fact that it is a minor, compoundable matter carrying a fine of just Rs 2,000. In practice, fresh action this long after the event is very unlikely."
Article Summary: The Bombay High Court has quashed a criminal case that had continued for 13 years against a man. The case arose from an allegation that the man had sold a 600-ml bottle of cold drink for Rs 26 even though its MRP was Rs 25. The man was working at his wife's shop when the incident took place.

Article Title: Apurva.ai opens AI platform to connect community voices, research
Article Text: Bengaluru: AI-enabled public-good digital infrastructure company Apurva.ai has expanded its Apurva LENS product into a platform designed to enable knowledge sharing and learning across organisations working on social and development challenges.Apurva.ai, a unit of C4EC Foundation co-founded by Nilekani Philanthropies, said the platform is being used and tested by organisations across the Global South. LENS has so far surfaced more than half a million voices and perspectives from the development ecosystem.The platform brings together research, evaluations, programme experience and conversations, while putting community voices and lived experiences at the centre. Organisations can retain control over what knowledge they keep private and what they choose to share.The move comes as development challenges become more complex, requiring govts, NGOs, funders and other organisations to build on knowledge generated across programmes and geographies rather than work in silos.Selco Foundation initially used LENS to bring together archival information, conversations and sector-focused material.The collaboration has since expanded through the Platform for Collective Wisdom, which connects community voices, practitioner perspectives and institutional knowledge across the development sector.Resilience Action Network Africa (RANA) used LENS to analyse community dialogues and research across Kenya, Uganda, Sierra Leone and South Africa, covering climate resilience, health, livelihoods, food systems, gender and governance.Infosys chairman and EkStep Foundation chairman Nandan Nilekani said, “Apurva.ai is bringing that thinking to knowledge — connecting research, organisational learning and community experience so that insights can travel across organisations and geographies.” Anand Rajan , co-founder and mission leader, Apurva.ai, said, “The development sector does not lack knowledge. It already exists across organisations, research, programmes and, importantly, within communities themselves. The challenge is turning all of this into understanding that people can act on.”LENS is now open for practitioners and organisations to explore, Apurva.ai said.
Article Summary: Apurva.ai has expanded its Apurva LENS product into a platform designed to enable knowledge sharing and learning. LENS has so far surfaced more than half a million voices and perspectives from the development ecosystem. The platform brings together research, evaluations, programme experience and conversations.

Article Title: Small-city ecomm surges, but order values trail big mkts
Article Text:
Fast delivery by scooter bike and van with mobile. E-commerce concept. Online food and shopping crate box order with route map. Webpage, app design. white brown background. vertical frame 3d render

BENGALURU: Online shopping is expanding beyond India’s biggest cities, but the value of those purchases remains concentrated in larger markets.Of more than 200 million orders processed in the last 12 months up to July this year, 57.2% originated outside the 96 largest cities, but these orders accounted for only 39.3% of total transaction value. Their average order value was Rs 830, less than half the Rs 1,714 recorded in the largest cities.EasyEcom, an ecommerce software company, compiled the data from transactions processed through marketplaces, brand websites, quick-commerce platforms, distributors and other channels connected to its system. Its customers include Borosil, Cred, Minimalist and Pilgrim, among others.The gap suggests that ecommerce growth outside the biggest cities is driven more by higher transaction volumes than by higher-value purchases. This could have implications for brands deciding where to hold inventory and how to manage deliveries across a wider network.The divide is even sharper at the state level. Of the 15 largest states in the dataset, 13 changed position when ranked by transaction value rather than order volume. Haryana moved from 11th by orders to third by value, supported by higher-value transactions in Gurugram and Sonipat. Its average order value of Rs 3,804 was more than six times Bihar ’s Rs 609. Bihar moved in the opposite direction, falling from 10th by volume to 15th by value.At the city level, Bengaluru was the largest market by order count, with around 11 million orders, 84% more than Mumbai. Gurugram ranked only seventh by volume but second by value, at Rs 1,848 crore. Its average order value of Rs 6,693 was more than four times Delhi’s Rs 1,499.“India’s commerce map has expanded much faster than its economics have converged,” said EasyEcom co-founder and CEO Punit Gupta.EasyEcom processed 112.3 million orders between February and July 2026, up 19.3% from 94.1 million in the preceding six months.
Article Summary: Of more than 200 million orders processed in the last 12 months up to July this year, 57.2% originated outside the 96 largest cities. But these orders accounted for only 39.3% of total transaction value. The gap suggests that ecommerce growth outside the biggest cities is driven more by higher transaction volumes than by higher-value purchases.

Article Title: Starbucks to set up GCC in Chennai
Article Text:

Article Title: Core sector growth at 3-mth low of 4.8%
Article Text:
Representative image

NEW DELHI: Core sector grew 4.8% in Aug, compared with 6.2% a year ago, official data released on Monday showed. Sequentially, the growth marked a slowdown from a downwardly revised figure of 5% in July and was at three-month low.Output in the energy dominant industries like natural gas (-4.9%), coal (-3.8%) and crude oil (-3.6%), barring the refinery products (2.6%), saw sequential contraction, reflecting the impact of the prolonged conflict in West Asia.On the other hand, output in the infrastructure dominant industries like steel (3.4%), cement (12.5%) and electricity (11.6%) showed positive growth in Aug.Output in the newly added iron ore industry decelerated (5.5%) during the month, while fertiliser output (-12.4%) contracted for the sixth consecutive month.Bank of Baroda chief economist Madan Sabnavis said higher growth in refinery products is due to exports and domestic consumption, while fertiliser production is down as sowing season slows and imports increase.The eight core sectors constitute 40.3% of the Index of Industrial Production (IIP), which measures output in the country's industrial sector, and is considered a bellwether for the latter's performance.
Article Summary: Core sector grew 4.8% in Aug, compared with 6.2% a year ago, official data showed. Sequentially, the growth marked a slowdown from a downwardly revised figure of 5% in July and was at three-month low.Output in the energy dominant industries like natural gas (-4.9%) and coal (-3.8%) saw sequential contraction. The eight core sectors constitute 40.3% of the Index of Industrial Production.

Article Title: GST rate rejig helps consumers upgrade
Article Text: NEW DELHI/MUMBAI: A year after GST rates were cut, automobile dispatches have continued to climb. Several two-wheeler users moved to four-wheelers as price cuts improved affordability, TV buyers have shifted towards larger sets and consumer goods volumes picked up in the Oct-Dec quarter, although they are now under pressure due to the West Asia crisis.Passenger vehicle dispatches reached a record 12.7 lakh units in April–June 2026, up 25.9% from a year earlier, according to Siam. Two-wheeler dispatches rose 20.3% to 56.3 lakh units. Siam has cited lower GST rates and easier financing among the factors supporting demand. Its figures measure supplies to dealers, rather than purchases by customers.Television shipments tell a different story. India’s smart TV shipments grew 10% year-on-year in Oct–Dec 2025, according to Counterpoint Research, before falling 3% in Jan-March 2026. TVs sized 55 inches and above were the fastest-growing category in the March quarter, accounting for nearly one-third of shipments.The trend, however, got stalled because of the uncertainty triggered by Operation Epic Fury US and Israel launched against Iran on Feb 28 and Counterpoint’s TV tracker recorded a 9.8% decline in shipments in April–June. GST on TVs above 32 inches, including 55-inch models, was slashed from 28% to 18% last Sept.Keshav Bansal, director at Intex Technologies, said the cut created “a meaningful affordability window” for bigger TVs. Intex’s consumer durables business grew 80% in FY26, with smart TVs among the drivers, he said. But “unit volumes have not risen in proportion to value growth; the more significant shift has been in product mix,” as buyers chose larger screens and better technology.Bansal said lower GST also supported air-conditioner demand, alongside a favourable summer and a lower comparison base. Rising input costs, including memory chips for TVs, and the cost of meeting newer energy-efficiency norms for ACs have since absorbed part of the tax benefit, he said.“In the long-term, it is definitely a positive, especially with people looking to move to branded products. But there is some impact in the short run due to the recent increase in input prices. Also, full refund of input tax credit will help in offsetting some of the cost,” said Liberty Shoes executive director Anupam Bansal.FMCG companies initially saw an improvement in demand after the rate changes. Volume growth picked up at companies, including Hindustan Unilever, Marico and Dabur. Nestlé India reported its strongest volume growth in five years in the Dec 2025 quarter, attributing it partly to a market recovery supported by GST benefits.That early lift has come under pressure as companies raised prices to offset higher costs. Companies and analysts are keeping a close watch on sales in the current quarter.
Article Summary: Passenger vehicle dispatches reached a record 12.7 lakh units in April–June 2026. Two-wheeler dispatches rose 20.3% to 56.3 lakh units. Siam has cited lower GST rates and easier financing among the factors supporting demand.

Article Title: MS expands India capacity for cloud and AI services
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Microsoft's new India South Central cloud region in Hyderabad is among its largest infrastructure investments in Asia, the company's India and South Asia president Puneet Chandok said, as it expands capacity for cloud and AI services.The facility is part of Microsoft's $20.5 billion investment commitment across Asia. Chandok did not disclose how much of that would be spent on which particular business interests. He said the expansion must account for the resources data centres consume and what surrounding communities gain. "How do you learn to build a data centre? It's by making sure that you're net accretive to the community," he told TOI, citing water, power and jobs.Chandok said advanced air cooling would eliminate water use for cooling at the new facilities. He also said Microsoft was replenishing water near its data centres and had committed to one gigawatt of green energy, of which 60 megawatts was already flowing. The company has not disclosed the new region's total power demand, making it difficult to assess those commitments against its expected resource use.Microsoft is pairing the infrastructure push with AI training, Chandok said.He put the number of people trained at 10 million and said close to 125,000 had secured jobs. The company also has more than 17,000 engineers across 10 Indian cities, he said.Speaking at the launch, MeitY secretary S Krishnan urged Microsoft to expand its development and research operations in India alongside its data centres. He said global investment in AI infrastructure should help build domestic capabilities in areas including AI servers and semiconductors, while creating higher-quality jobs. Krishnan argued that future data centres should be located closer to electricity-generation centres, rather than concentrated around connectivity hubs.
Article Summary: Microsoft's new India South Central cloud region in Hyderabad is among its largest infrastructure investments in Asia. The facility is part of Microsoft's $20.5 billion investment commitment across Asia. Microsoft is pairing the infrastructure push with AI training, Chandok said.

Article Title: Govt winds up telecom commission
Article Text:
(Representative image)

NEW DELHI: Govt has with immediate effect dissolved its apex decision-making body for telecom and digital communication - digital communications commission (DCC), which was originally established as telecom commission in 1989, before being renamed in 2018. The communication ministry's department of telecommunication (DoT) notified this decision through a Sept 19, 2026 resolution that was published in the Gazette of India. "With effect from date of publication of this resolution, the DCC shall stand dissolved," says the gazette.Decisions for projects up to Rs 100 crore can be taken by the secretary DoT, up to Rs 500 crore by the telecom minister and those above Rs 500 crore to Rs 1,000 crore were considered by the DCC. Now the same will be referred to the expenditure finance committee.
Article Summary: Decisions for projects up to Rs 100 crore can be taken by the secretary DoT. Those above Rs 500 crore to Rs 1,000 crore were considered by the DCC. Now the same will be referred to the expenditure finance committee.

Article Title: NSE IPO subscribed 5.7x, generates Rs 90.2k crore demand
Article Text:
NSE IPO

MUMBAI: The Rs 22,568-crore NSE IPO was subscribed 5.7 times the bidding amount, generating a total demand worth nearly Rs 90,200 crore. While the institutional part was subscribed 12.7 times, the HNI part was subscribed 6.6 times and the retail part 1.4 times, data on BSE showed. The part reserved for employees was subscribed 2.4 times. About 38.5 lakh applications were received in the IPO, an NSE release said.Before bidding opened, merchant bankers had allotted nearly 3.8 crore NSE shares to about 189 institutional investors at a price of Rs 1,785 per share, raising Rs 6,746 crore. The issue received total bids for 50.6 crore shares against 8.9 crore shares that were offered, exchange data showed. With Rs 22,568 crore raised, NSE IPO is now the second-largest such offer in India.
Article Summary: The Rs 22,568-crore NSE IPO was subscribed 5.7 times the bidding amount. About 38.5 lakh applications were received in the IPO. The issue received total bids for 50.6 crore shares against 8.9 crore shares that were offered.
